summary: IDS feed s144_double is degraded with 2 high-severity faults: 8.5% jumbo frames (up to 8058B) exceed the 1Gbps IDS port's 1518B MTU and are dropped at NIC, and microbursts peak at 2.78 Gbps (278% of port capacity) causing overload drops. Both cause packet loss before IDS inspection, severely reducing detection coverage.

findings.root_cause: Network forwards jumbo frames up to 8058 bytes but the IDS tool port/NIC is limited to standard 1518-byte Ethernet MTU without jumbo support. Packet broker passes frames unchanged, so the IDS NIC drops them on ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS drops 163 of 1908 frames (8.5%) at the NIC before inspection. As this IDS needs full payload, it is blind to large-frame flows and will miss exploits/malware carried in those packets.

recommended_fix.why: Tool requires full payload so slicing/trimming to 1518B is not an option. Enable 9000B jumbo MTU on IDS NIC/capture stack and ensure packet broker preserves jumbo frames, or filter/redirect jumbo flows to a jumbo-capable tool port.

findings.root_cause: All traffic is aggregated to a single 1 Gbps IDS port without load balancing. Bursty traffic creates 1ms microbursts peaking at 2.78 Gbps (278% of capacity) across 9 intervals, exceeding the 80% overload threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS port buffers overflow and drops packets during bursts. Flow reassembly fails, IDS misses attacks under load, and detection coverage is incomplete precisely when traffic volume is highest.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 3+ IDS ports or upgrade to 10Gbps tool port with 5-tuple load balancing to absorb 2.78 Gbps bursts and keep per-port utilization below 80%.
